sources.ref: O-1/O-3 2026-10-03: nl_only ask wording + fixed disclosure line
UX_Feedback_v4 item 13 (2026-10-05): the two seats' social replies must not be near-identical pleasantries

notes: v5 (2026-10-18, owner+student direction): level-keyed social pools — social_high (terse/strained) and social_low (relaxed) selected by the speaker's recorded check-in level; base social pool remains for nopress/pre-check-in.
Historical wording preserved for reference profiles only. Contains busy/stuck language ('bit swamped', 'stuck on') that can interfere with a pressure manipulation (spec §7.3); not for pilot profiles.

v2 (UX round 3, AI-1/AI-2): warmer social lines so a pleasantry is answered like a coworker would, and more multiword variety per rule so the session no-repeat draw (engines.social_fallback) rarely falls through to the short defaults.

v3 (O-1/O-3): asks_intel_nl invites a typed crate ask where no picker exists; identity_probe is the fixed truthful disclosure for 'are you a bot/real?' probes (answered before generation, never model text).

v4 (UX round 4, item 13): the social pool mixes one pleasantry-with-return-question with topically distinct task-state lines, so two seats replying to the same pleasantry cannot converge on two paraphrases of 'doing alright'.
